references.note: Read sections 1 and 8 in Elizabeth Carter’s translation. Compare the discipline of distinguishing one’s actions from external circumstances, and of receiving events as they occur, with this compilation’s active effort and prayerful trust. Attend to the different accounts of human freedom and relationship with God.

subjects.displayTitle: Consultation: thinking together and acting in unity
subjects.introduction: The spark, ‘Abdu’l-Bahá says, comes when flint and steel strike together: truth shows itself in the clash of differing opinions, not in the victory of one of them. Consultation begins with a small act of release. An opinion is offered as a contribution rather than defended as a possession, and if someone else’s view proves truer it is accepted at once, with gratitude rather than hurt. Bahá’u’lláh calls consultation the lamp of guidance, one of the two luminaries of the heaven of divine wisdom beside compassion, and He extends it into every matter, from a family choosing a children’s teacher to an assembly weighing a community’s welfare. It asks for purity of motive, humility, patience and love, and for the discipline to speak with complete freedom and then stand behind the decision reached, so that experience can show whether it was sound. The Qur’an sets mutual counsel beside prayer and generosity as a mark of those who answer God [1]. From here the way opens into the diversity of thought that enriches a community, the love and fellowship among the friends that keeps it whole, and the spiritual assemblies and gatherings where thinking together becomes a shared way of life.
subjects.arc: Begin with releasing attachment to an opinion, establish truth-seeking and spiritual qualities, consider disagreement and decision, then follow consultation into institutions, practical responsibilities, and shared learning.

order.why: Open with offering an opinion as a contribution and accepting a better view.
shortened: He who expresses an opinion should not voice it as correct and right but set it forth as a contribution to the consensus of opinion, for the light of reality becomes apparent when two opinions coincide. A spark is produced when flint and steel come together. Man should weigh his opinions with the utmost serenity, calmness and composure. Before expressing his own views he should carefully consider the views already advanced by others. If he finds that a previously expressed opinion is more true and worthy, he should accept it immediately and not willfully hold to an opinion of his own.

order.why: Make gratitude for reasoned objection part of the search for truth.
Read free expression and the clash of differing opinions.
Consider the reported warning against a chalice filled with self.
Keep the reported invitation to investigate reality in fellowship.
shortened: Let no one assert and insist upon his own mere opinion; nay, rather, let each investigate reality with the greatest love and fellowship. Consult upon every matter, and when one presents the point of view of reality itself, that shall be acceptable to all.

order.why: Ground the practice in spiritual qualities.
shortened: The prime requisites for them that take counsel together are purity of motive, radiance of spirit, detachment from all else save God, attraction to His Divine Fragrances, humility and lowliness amongst His loved ones, patience and long-suffering in difficulties and servitude to His exalted Threshold. Should they be graciously aided to acquire these attributes, victory from the unseen Kingdom of Bahá shall be vouchsafed to them.

order.why: Read consultation and compassion as the two luminaries of wisdom.
Keep the related lamp-of-guidance formulation.
shortened: The heaven of divine wisdom is illumined with two luminaries: consultation and compassion. In all matters hold fast unto consultation, for it is the lamp of guidance that leadeth the way and bestoweth understanding.

order.why: Read the address to Jamal that repeats the principle.
shortened: O Jamal, fix thy gaze upon this decisive, firm and blessed word which hath been recorded by the Supreme Pen in the Crimson Book: The heaven of divine wisdom is illumined with two luminaries: consultation and compassion. In all things hold fast unto consultation, for it is the lamp of guidance that leadeth the way and bestoweth understanding.

order.why: Retain the concise lamp image.
Place consultation within the Ishraqat’s wider social principles.
Keep the related address concerning consultation, kindness, and order.
Consider consultation with vigilance for public welfare and safety.
Read the ladder of collective well-being.
Read reverence and universal benevolence as foundations.
shortened: The foundation of consultation is among the greatest divine institutions, but it must be based on the fear of God and universal benevolence.

order.why: Connect friendly consultation with bettering the world.
shortened: With the utmost friendliness and in a spirit of perfect fellowship take ye counsel together, and dedicate the precious days of your lives to the betterment of the world and the promotion of the Cause of Him Who is the Ancient and Sovereign Lord of all.

order.why: Read meetings as a means of fellowship and human oneness.
shortened: With utmost joy and fragrance gather in the merciful meeting and consult about every matter so that gathering may become the cause of fellowship, love and oneness of the human world.

order.why: Trace fellowship, unity, gathering, and rectification of affairs.
shortened: Praise be to the Intended One Who, through His sacred will, has bestowed perfect fellowship between the hearts and souls of all people, and from this fellowship complete unity is achieved, and this unity is the most mighty door for the tranquility of nations, and through this unity gathering is made manifest, and gathering is the cause and reason for the rectification of all affairs through consultation, whose decree has been sent down with utmost clarity in the [Divine] Book.

order.why: Keep service and continuing agreement together.
shortened: O friends! When the intention is service to the Sacred Threshold and perpetual, continuous unity and agreement are achieved, it will become light upon light and the hosts of divine confirmation will surround that gathering from all directions.

order.why: Join agreement and prayer.
shortened: It behoveth you to seek agreement and to be united; it behoveth you to be in close communion one with the other, at one both in body and soul, till ye match the Pleiades or a string of lustrous pearls.

Whenever ye enter the council-chamber, recite this prayer with a heart throbbing with the love of God and a tongue purified from all but His remembrance, that the All-Powerful may graciously aid you to achieve supreme victory:
O God, my God! We are servants of Thine that have turned with devotion to Thy Holy Face, that have detached ourselves from all besides Thee in this glorious Day.

order.why: Read the prayerful account of a gathering reaching a decision.
shortened: They gathered in the assembly of glory, in thy name, the Merciful, the Compassionate. They consulted concerning the mighty Testament; agreed upon the right decision and were confirmed with a new spirit.

order.why: Keep the affirmation of luminous consultation.
Consider why several counsels can exceed one person’s view.
shortened: Regarding consultation that is commanded - you had asked about this. The purpose of consultation is to show that the views of several individuals are assuredly preferable to one man, even as the power of a number of men is of course greater than the power of one man. Thus consultation is acceptable in the presence of the Almighty, and hath been enjoined upon the believers, so that they may confer upon ordinary and personal matters, as well as on affairs which are general in nature and universal.

order.why: Read the parallel account of combined strength.
Acknowledge the limits of an individual’s foresight.
shortened: No individual alone can understand the consequences of matters or know what is needed today or have the correct opinion. If it were such that each person had absolute authority and could carry out whatever they deemed good, the entire structure of affairs would completely fall apart, matters would become disordered, and both outward and spiritual chaos would ensue.

order.why: Seek depth and appropriateness.
Consider movement from conjecture toward certitude.
shortened: Consultation increaseth awareness and transformeth conjecture into certitude. It is a shining light in the dark world - it guideth and directeth. For everything there hath been and shall be a state of maturity and perfection. The maturity and manifestation of understanding becometh evident through consultation.'

order.why: Connect the collision of thoughts with discovery and progress.
shortened: In truth, consultation is among the greatest characteristics of this Dispensation. The people of Baha must keep consultation in view in all important matters and consider this significant matter as an assured good. Especially in matters that concern everyone, such consultation is service to the Truth, and such collision of thoughts leads to the discovery of what is necessary and fitting.

The foundation of progress in all degrees of existence is consultation, and until this is firmly established, affairs will not revolve around their desired axis. Great care is needed in this regard, such that even in minor matters the friends must consult with one another.

order.why: Allow time, reflection, calmness, and repeated deliberation.
Keep the prudent and friendly gathering.
shortened: It is incumbent upon the loved ones of God to exercise the greatest care and prudence in all things, whether great or small, to take counsel together and unitedly resist the onslaught of the stirrers up of strife and the movers of mischief. They must endeavour to consort in a friendly spirit with everyone, must follow moderation in their conduct, must have respect and consideration one for another and show loving-kindness and tender regard to all the peoples of the world.

order.why: Join gathering wise people, planning, and trust.
shortened: Similarly in general matters, when a difficulty arises and hardship occurs, the wise ones should gather, consult together and make a plan, then trust in God and submit to destiny, so that divine assistance may help in whatever way manifests. Consultation is among the definitive commands of the Lord of creation.

order.why: Consider outcomes and benefit to the world.
shortened: In all matters one must consult while considering the outcome. Take what is good and what benefits the world - this is My bidding before and after.

order.why: Read the fuller assembly counsel, including free expression, decision, and united action.
shortened: They must in every matter search out the truth and not insist upon their own opinion, for stubbornness and persistence in one's views will lead ultimately to discord and wrangling and the truth will remain hidden. The honored members must with all freedom express their own thoughts, and it is in no wise permissible for one to belittle the thought of another, nay, he must with moderation set forth the truth, and should differences of opinion arise a majority of voices must prevail, and all must obey and submit to the majority. It is again not permitted that any one of the honored members object to or censure, whether in or out of the meeting, any decision arrived at previously, though that decision be not right, for such criticism would prevent any decision from being enforced.

order.why: Keep the reported preference for unanimity alongside majority decision.
Read the paraphrased account of a five-to-four decision after loving exchange.
Consider the need to reach a decision suited to circumstances.
shortened: Whatever you consider appropriate and suitable to the time, place and circumstances, implement it by majority vote. For if matters, especially in the gathering of the Hands of the Cause of God, are not decided upon, that gathering will become completely weak and foundationless, and many problems will arise. Inevitably different opinions will emerge and affairs will fall into disorder.

order.why: Connect consultation with acting upon its result.
Read obedience to assembly decisions in the stated concern about disorder.
Keep the direct instruction to implement a decision.
Read the call to put principles into practice.
shortened: Add as much as ye can to love and affinity and produce ye among yourselves unity and agreement. Put ye in practice the principles of consultation.

order.why: Consider silence as a response to escalating contention.
shortened: If anyone rises in opposition and dispute, maintain complete silence, for if one responds in kind, it will surely lead to ill-feeling, and ill-feeling breeds anger and intensity, and anger and passionate feelings lead to error.

order.why: Keep the reported concern that opposition can intensify resistance.
shortened: You must be careful not to have anyone harmed by speaking. Suppose some speak not well. Do not oppose him; merely let him know his speech was not pleasant, no discussion. If a thing is not pleasing, keep silence. Do not express pleasure. Opposing causes resistance and that will cause division.

order.why: Read the reported counsel against creating differences after a decision.
Preserve the particular account of silence when interventions increased differences.
shortened: However, upon reflection it was deemed inexpedient at this time and therefore was not sent, for it was observed that whatever we attempted to remove differences among the friends became the cause of their increase. Therefore, there is no remedy save silence.

order.why: Keep the specific procedure for renewed consultation in its historical setting.
Read the reported assembly’s purpose as service to people.
Connect assembly responsibilities with needy people and children’s education.
shortened: Give great importance to the consultative assembly. All must show perfect obedience and submission to whatever proceeds from the consultative assembly, for the duty of the consultative assembly is to preserve, protect and arrange the means of livelihood for the needy and the education of children. The friends of God must accept and obey such matters with heart and soul.

order.why: Read the qualifications of elected members and teachers’ consultation with them.
Retain the reported distinction between convention representatives and other attendees.
shortened: Abdul Baha: The object is that all affairs ought to be referred to the Convention, that is the Assembly which is composed of the representatives from the different assemblies sent to the Convention, not all the people gathered for the meetings. If all people present in the meetings take part in the discussions it would not do.

order.why: Read the reported division between decisions and their execution.
Keep the historical arrangement involving men’s and women’s assemblies.
Read the particular distinction between a devotional gathering and a consultative board.
shortened: But all of their mention and thought in their meeting should be confined to teaching the truth, and to constantly persuade people in pure and divine brilliancy and in absolute godlike spirituality. They should not interfere with the affairs which have regard to the Board of Consultation, because confusion of thought conduces to division and causes disturbance to the mind, and then pure spirituality would cease.

By this it is intended that the assembly of the maid-servants of the Merciful should be with pure spirituality and with absolute brilliancy, and become a torch of that blessed fire, a center of the merciful feelings.

order.why: Keep the instruction on spiritual consultation in its setting.
shortened: With regard to the assembly, there must be spiritual consultation therein; discourses about the manifestation of the Greatest Orb, the effulgence of the Sun of Reality, the greatness of the blessed Cause, the power and penetration of the Word of God, the might of the divine Covenant and Testament must be mentioned.
Every discussion besides this, will not give complete results.

order.why: Connect gatherings with education of the rising generation.
shortened: They establish assemblies and gatherings and their affairs are conducted through consultation among them for the exaltation of Thy Word and the education of the successful rising generation to establish Thy proofs and evidence, and the instruction of youth in the proofs and tidings that have preceded from the blessed souls who unveiled the mysteries of the Day of Thy Manifestation.

order.why: Read the reported convention’s humanitarian and teaching purposes.
shortened: For example if during such days a Great Consultative Baha'i Convention were to be organized, its results would be infinite. Each session must be devoted to the consideration of various vital topics and humanitarian principles, and several sessions be devoted to the discussion of the way and means for spreading the Cause in different parts of the world and declaring the Glad-tidings of the Kingdom to all mankind.

order.why: Keep the reported invitation to leaders to discuss enduring benefits.
shortened: As they are days of freedom from work and worry the leaders of communities must discuss such problems which may be beneficial to the individuals and the outcomes of which be eternal.

order.why: Read the historical account of ministers’ concentrated deliberations.
shortened: The space at these gatherings would belong to the ministers alone; even their attendants were not permitted to be present. Bringing to bear the full measure of their concentration, and animated by a spirit of abundant joy and perfect concord, these ministers would consult on matters of great importance.

They would dedicate an entire night or more to the discussion of each matter. When they would conclude their deliberations, such that they all regarded the subsequent course of action as having been decisively established, they would put their decision in writing.

order.why: Preserve the reported account of a society using signs without words.
Keep the brief report of differences within a board without inventing its continuation.
Bring loving consultation into marriage.
Read mutual assistance in national needs.
shortened: Resolve all matters, both small and great, through consultation. Do not undertake any important matter without consultation. Think of one another, assist in each other's affairs, share in each other's sorrows. Leave none of the nation's people in need. Help one another so that all may unitedly and harmoniously become as one body.

order.why: Consider the practical decision about a children’s teacher.
Keep the question of renting a meeting hall.
Read consultation about a Mashriqu’l-Adhkar site.
shortened: As for the matter of the Mashriqu'l-Adhkar, come together with the friends in utmost love and unity, consult and delve into this matter and reach a unanimous decision, and submit a request to the Government for a site.

order.why: Retain the decision about a memorial trace in the Mashriqu’l-Adhkar.
Read the agreed increase in teaching meetings.
shortened: Thou hadst given the glad tidings that at a gathering held at the home of Aqa Siyyid Hasan, consultation took place regarding the increase of teaching meetings, and complete agreement was reached that nine meetings should be added and established in various locations.

order.why: Keep the appointment of a local teacher through consultation.
shortened: In every land the friends must consult together and appoint someone from among the people of that land for the purpose of teaching.

order.why: Read gathering for the exaltation of the Word.
shortened: The loved ones must gather together in wisdom and take counsel regarding the exaltation of the Most Great Word.

order.why: Follow consultation through amendments and approval of a company charter.
Keep the hope for a company sustained by consultation.
shortened: May they form an assembly composed of blessed souls so that affairs may be carried out through consultation, and unlike other companies, may its duration not be brief.

order.why: Read the instruction to obtain partners’ views.
Consider consensual assistance from surplus income without making it obligatory.
Keep the storehouse decision as a concrete application.
Read the Minister’s efforts in their stated historical setting.
Retain the particular proposal about assistance in Alexandretta.
Read the consultation behind a decision to remain in a place.
shortened: Regarding what was written about the beloved of the heart, his eminence the Observer, upon him be 9 66 [Baha'u'llah] and His favors, and his stay, and likewise what the spiritual friend his eminence Aqa 'Azizu'llah, upon him be 9 66 [Baha'u'llah] eternally, related - their stay in that land has been accepted, since in all correspondences the command of consultation was mentioned, and as the collective opinion settled upon this and purely for the sake of God their stay emerged from consultation, therefore it was adorned with the ornament of acceptance.

order.why: Consider residence and occupation decided through consultation.
shortened: As to the previous question regarding where they should reside and what they should do, these matters have been referred to consultation, as is recorded in the divine Tablets. One must consult with steadfast, assured souls and act accordingly. That which proceedeth from consultation is best for him who holdeth fast unto wisdom in the kingdom of creation.

order.why: Explains consultation as a means of gaining insight in matters great and small.
Keep the counsel concerning the recipient’s affairs.
Read personal counsel beside the binding principle.
shortened: This matter too was mentioned purely for the good of all, otherwise the law of consultation is binding and all must hold fast to it and act upon it. It would also be beloved if your honor were to meet with some and consult regarding your affairs.

order.why: Consider consultation about occupation.
shortened: Consult outwardly with the friends in that land, and occupy thyself with whatever they deem advisable.

order.why: Keep the assembly’s particular decision.
Read deliberation followed by implementation.
Retain the request to send the decision.
shortened: O ye beloved friends of 'Abdu'l-Baha! Should you observe that through a general election the Spiritual Assembly will gain increased influence and no one will have cause for objection or hesitation, and all will acknowledge the decisions of the Spiritual Assembly, in such case a general election would be better and more fitting.
Consult ye regarding this matter and send the result of your decision.

order.why: Keep the cited sacred tradition in its attributed voice.
shortened: In the sacred tradition, His Holiness the Prophet, peace be upon Him, says: "Whatever the believers deem good, that is good in the sight of God." Therefore, whatever the friends consider advisable, carry that out.

order.why: Consider discretion where publicity could endanger people.
shortened: To hold fast to wisdom is obligatory and essential, and likewise consultation, but in some matters consultation becomes a cause of notoriety, and this is contrary to wisdom and the protection of certain souls.

order.why: Read the caution about informants and timing in its particular setting.
shortened: Let that honored friend convey this greatest glad-tidings to them. In all circumstances, all must observe wisdom. When any name is mentioned at the Divine Throne, the rains of remembrance descend particularly for that one from the heaven of divine mercy, but the friends must observe the time and not let go of wisdom. Often someone claims love deceitfully, intending only to gather information, and God veils this, for the tale-bearer has ever been and will ever be detested.
But the friends must look with the light of God and not open their lips until they observe the radiance of glory in a face.

order.why: Keep the requirement that consultation accord with wisdom.
Read association and gatherings under the same counsel of wisdom.
Join wisdom and consultation.
Keep the relation of union, wisdom, and counsel.
shortened: As to what thou didst mention regarding union and connection - We have commanded the loved ones of God to consult concerning all matters, and the wisdom which We have revealed its decree in the Scriptures and Tablets.

order.why: Read the response to differences through love and fellowship.
shortened: In reply to Abdul-Husayn's letter, write: Regarding what was mentioned about differences between the friends - all are obligated by the Divine Tablets to demonstrate love, unity, affection and fellowship, which are the cause of exalting the Word of God, and they must act accordingly.

order.why: Consider the contrast with action driven by self and passion.
shortened: We have ordained that every matter be resolved through consultation, and this binding decree hath repeatedly flowed from the Most Exalted Pen in Scriptures and Tablets. Nevertheless, some act without consultation, rather in mere obedience to self and passion, doing that which hath been and is the cause of grief to God's loved ones.

order.why: Keep the instruction to consult designated and assured souls.
Read qualities of those with whom one consults.
shortened: He saith: "The heaven of divine wisdom is illumined with two luminaries: consultation and compassion." In every matter consult with souls who are assured, tranquil, content and pleasing to God, and act upon that which is found preferable.

order.why: Retain the specific counsel to consult Afnan.
Distinguish a particular recommendation from an absolute command.
shortened: The one true God has commanded His servants to engage in consultation, that all may hold fast to His cord and act accordingly.

The counsel that shone forth from the horizon of the will of the Lord of all beings was not given as an absolute command, but rather was offered purely out of wisdom and goodwill. Whatever appears beneficial after consultation may be acted upon.

order.why: Read reflection before action.
shortened: In any case, time is needed - it must be made so firm that no thought of change would occur. Then whatever is expedient, after reflection and consultation, carry it out.

order.why: Keep the brief approval of consultation.
Connect consultation and subsequent action.
Read the blessing associated with carrying out a decision.
shortened: Consultation in matters is most beloved, and acting upon it after a decision emerges has ever been and continues to be the cause of blessing and good.

order.why: Retain the compact affirmation of consultation.
Keep endorsement of the resulting judgment.
Read the general statement of the principle.
shortened: God hath ordained all matters to be resolved through consultation.

order.why: Place the gathering’s intention and acceptance in its theological setting.
shortened: Outwardly, these matters depend upon consultation. In truth, let several souls gather together for the sake of God, and whatsoever appeareth from consultation, whether there or here, let them hold fast unto it. The principle of consultation hath ever been and is acceptable before God, and in the Books of both past and present this firm decree hath been revealed from the Presence of the All-Wise. His is the command, and ours is submission and obedience. His is the decree, and ours is acceptance and compliance. He is the Ruler in the beginning and in the end.

order.why: Keep patience and presence alongside consultation.
shortened: He says, exalted be His glory:
"May he be patient; may he be present; may he hold fast to consultation and act according to what emerges from it.

order.why: Read counsel to consult and proceed.
Join consultation to trusting action.
shortened: Time and again they commanded me to convey to you that they should consult on matters and then, trusting in God, act accordingly.

order.why: Read the instruction to consult before entering a matter.
Let consultation as wisdom’s fruit lead into trust.
shortened: O 'Ali-Qabli-Akbar! The fruit of the tree of insight and wisdom is consultation. Take counsel in matters, and when thou hast decided, place thy trust in God, the Single, the Strong, the Almighty.

order.why: Preserve the wider passage on seeking and detachment as contextual material.
shortened: How many were the Alexanders of bygone ages and centuries who, with the utmost endeavor and effort, ran in search of the fountain of life but found it not. Now its seas are manifest and surging in the realm of possibility, and yet true seekers are rare to find. Until the fire of search is kindled, the door of bounty will not open.

order.why: Open the supplied readings with Shoghi Effendi’s summary of the principle.
Read the supplied synthesis of qualities, liberty, investigation, and decision.
shortened: Love and harmony, purity of motive, humility and lowliness amongst the friends, patience and long-suffering in difficulties -- these inform the attitude with which they proceed "with the utmost devotion, courtesy, dignity, care and moderation to express their views", each using "perfect liberty" both in so doing and in "unveiling the proof of his demonstration". "If another contradicts him, he must not become excited because if there be no investigation or verification of questions and matters, the agreeable view will not be discovered neither understood." "The shining spark of truth cometh forth only after the clash of differing opinions." If unanimity is not subsequently achieved, decisions are arrived at by majority vote.

order.why: Consider freedom of speech and its responsibilities.
Read the rejection of individual assertions as authoritative criteria.
Keep the supplied account of unanimity, voting, and collective ownership.
shortened: The ideal of Baha'i consultation is to arrive at a unanimous decision. When this is not possible a vote must be taken. In the words of the beloved guardian: "... when they are called upon to arrive at a certain decision, they should, after dispassionate, anxious and cordial consultation, turn to God in prayer, and with earnestness and conviction and courage record their vote and abide by the voice of the majority, which we are told by the Master to be the voice of truth, never to be challenged and always to be whole-heartedly enforced." As soon as a decision is reached it becomes the decision of the whole Assembly, not merely of those members who happened to be among the majority....

order.why: Read the supplied Tablet’s account of those chosen to consult.
Make reconsideration through experience explicit alongside support for decisions.
Distinguish solving a problem from the group confession described in this letter.
Connect continued exchange of views to collective interests.
Keep teaching efforts coordinated with assemblies.
Read institutional work and individual initiative together.
Explore individual initiative beside participation in collective endeavors.
Close with the supplied Christian passage on agreement and gathering in the divine name.

questions: What changes when an opinion is offered for shared examination rather than defended as a personal possession?
How can a group make room for both candid disagreement and a spirit of love?
What do these readings suggest about the relation between spiritual qualities and practical procedures?
How might wholehearted support for a decision enable the learning needed to reconsider it?
What does the Qur’anic association of counsel, prayer, and generosity add to this discussion of communal responsibility?
How would consultation differ across a family, a voluntary gathering, and an authorized assembly, and which qualities should remain present in each?

references.label: 1 · Qur’an 42:38 · Counsel, prayer, and generosity
references.note: Compare the verse’s association of response to God, prayer, mutual counsel, and giving with the spiritual and practical responsibilities in this compilation. The parallel translations permit attention to how counsel is expressed. Keep the verse distinct from the particular institutional procedures described in the Baha’i readings.
